top_repositories.recommendation_reason: This is the best fit for a beginner who wants to reproduce a practical LangGraph AI Agent project within 8 hours. It is explicitly beginner-oriented, has a small and clear project structure, focuses on one concrete Weather & Travel Assistant use case, and includes tool calling, persistent memory, a step-by-step tutorial, and a workflow diagram. It meets all must-have requirements and is easier to scope than a broad multi-phase tutorial repository.
tradeoffs: Requires three external API keys, which adds setup friction for a beginner.
Very low community engagement and only a single commit reduce external validation.
Some implementation files appear thin, so the depth of LangGraph graph construction may be limited.
Actual end-to-end runnability is not fully confirmed by the supplied evidence.
learning_path: Read the README Quick Start and the step-by-step tutorial first to understand prerequisites, API key requirements, installation commands, and the intended agent behavior.
Inspect the state definition and workflow graph construction first, using state.py and workflow.py, to map how LangGraph nodes, edges, and state flow are organized.
Then inspect agent_logic.py plus the tools and models directories to understand how weather lookup, web search, and persistent memory are connected to the graph.
Run run_agent.py with a simple weather query first, then try a travel-planning query and observe how tool calling and memory affect the workflow.
After the basic flow works, review how errors or missing API keys affect execution and document the minimum configuration needed to reproduce the agent locally.

ranking.final_reason: The deterministic top score belongs to ShadowQuill/langchain-langgraph-tutorial, but the scores are close and the user's constraints emphasize beginner difficulty, a practical AI Agent project, simple structure, and reproduction within 8 hours. eliharoun/langgraph-weather-agent is the better first choice because it is explicitly beginner-oriented, small, focused on one concrete weather/travel assistant use case, and includes a step-by-step tutorial and workflow diagram. ShadowQuill remains valuable as a broader LangGraph curriculum and reference, while sujeetgund/awesome-langgraph is best used later for exploring additional LangGraph patterns.
